title: MetaCan screening output, rubric v3.1
description: The output contract for every screening run under rubric v3.1. This document QUOTES the rubric; it never paraphrases it. Where a description below restates a rule, the wording is copied from docs/protocol/rubric-v3.md, because the schema misquoting the rubric is D24 and two documents that disagree are two instruments (D20). pilot/check_instrument.R fails the build if this file and the rubric disagree about any field, in either direction. The legacy screening-schema.json remains ONLY so that v1 and v2 label files stay readable; no new screening validates against it.

id.description: The OpenAlex work id, exactly as given in the payload.

categories.description: Every category the work belongs to; a work may carry more than one, and categories are not ranked and none is primary. An EMPTY array is OUT, which means 'in no defined category', not 'near the important one'. insufficient_payload means the record cannot be screened (a scraping artifact as a title, boilerplate in the abstract field, a title and abstract from different papers, spam) and is reported, never silently dropped.

domain.description: REQUIRED when categories contains metaresearch, and null otherwise. Taken verbatim from Ioannidis's five thematic areas: methods, reporting, reproducibility, evaluation, and incentives (how to do, report, verify, correct, and reward science).

study_design.description: Coded for every work, from this vocabulary and no other. not_applicable means the work is not empirical research: editorials, datasets, software.

genre.description: One vocabulary, defined in the rubric, and this schema QUOTES that list rather than paraphrasing it.

about_ca_system.description: ABOUT_CA_SYSTEM: the Canadian research system or academy is a substantive object. A Canadian institution as setting is not this.

about_ca_topic.description: ABOUT_CA_TOPIC: Canada is a substantive subject, whether or not research is the object.

confidence.description: If the abstract is missing, judge on the title alone and set confidence to low unless the title is unambiguous. low is a legitimate answer: a screener that never says low is not being careful; it is being confident.

reason.description: One sentence naming the rubric rule the decision rests on.
